data.narrative: Completed Module 1 'Reading Requirements' learning about extracting explicit/implicit/conflicting requirements from ambiguous prose, choosing categorized matrix structure for requirements, identifying cancellation contradiction between spec sections, and proposing two concrete resolution options.

dimension_scores.observation: Extracted 22 requirements across USER/PROVIDER/PLATFORM stakeholders with functional/constraint/quality attribute types, including 12 ambiguities and identifying missing authentication, platform support, and payout mechanics
dimension_scores.evidence: artifacts/requirements/module-01-full-extraction.md contains 22 requirements with type, stakeholder, source, confidence ratings

dimension_scores.observation: Identified 5 requirements affected by blocked cancellation decision (payment flow, earnings display, pricing autonomy, vetting process), showing understanding of requirement interdependencies
dimension_scores.evidence: Requirements document includes 'Affected Requirements' section mapping cancellation decision impact

dimension_scores.observation: Flagged cancellation requirement as BLOCKED pending PM decision with two concrete resolution options (platform-first universal policy vs provider policy with platform floor), demonstrating proactive risk identification
dimension_scores.evidence: progress/decomposition-execution-planning/module1_fix.md contains two implementable options with tradeoffs

dimension_scores.observation: Each requirement includes clear statement, type, stakeholder, source, and confidence rating, making them actionable for engineers
dimension_scores.evidence: All 22 requirements follow consistent format with type, stakeholder, source, confidence

dimension_scores.observation: Responded to spec contradiction by proposing two concrete buildable options with tradeoffs rather than just flagging the problem, showing ability to adapt to changing requirements
dimension_scores.evidence: module1_fix.md provides Option 1 (platform-first, simple) and Option 2 (provider policy with floor, complex)

dimension_scores.observation: Identified tension between provider autonomy (set own availability) and scale requirement (handle few thousand users) that forces design decision on concurrency handling
dimension_scores.evidence: Break step analysis recognized tension between simplicity and scale requirements

strengths: Extracted 22 requirements going beyond surface level to find implicit requirements and missing topics
Chose categorized matrix structure making gaps visible by stakeholder and type
Identified cancellation contradiction and proposed two concrete resolution options with tradeoffs
Flagged 12 specific ambiguities including authentication, platform support, payout timing, and analytics scope
data.recommendation: Validate requirements with PM before proceeding to dependency mapping in Module 2 - some implicit requirements may be wrong and ambiguities may have obvious answers not visible to engineering

public_evidence.student_action: Extracted 22 requirements from SkillSwap spec using categorized matrix structure with type, stakeholder, source, and confidence ratings for each
public_evidence.technical_detail: Document includes USER/PROVIDER/PLATFORM stakeholders with functional/constraint/quality attribute types, 12 flagged ambiguities, and 5 requirements affected by blocked cancellation decision
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Demonstrates ability to read ambiguous specs and extract actionable requirements while identifying gaps and contradictions before they become costly rework

public_evidence.student_action: Identified contradiction between provider autonomy and platform universal cancellation policy, proposed two concrete buildable options with tradeoffs

public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows ability to identify spec contradictions and propose concrete solutions rather than just flagging problems, critical for preventing misaligned work

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Used verb pass for functional requirements, qualifier pass for constraints/quality attributes, silence pass to find missing topics like authentication and platform support
Chose Option B grouping by stakeholder (user/provider/platform) AND type (functional/constraint/quality attribute) to make gaps visible
Identified binary contradiction in cancellation policy and tension between provider autonomy and scale requirements

learning_style_signals: prefers structured categorization and concrete examples
